\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{عقبة} (ʿaqaba)}{عقبة (ʿaqaba)}]{\ar{عقبة} (ʿaqaba) — an obstacle}

\label{lesson:AR-C372-aqaba}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to contribute, then the Arabic for an incentive.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{عقبة}}
\textbf{\ar{عقبة}} — \emph{ʿaqaba} — \textquotedblleft{}an obstacle\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{كانت} \ar{اللغة} \ar{أكبر} \ar{عقبة} \ar{أمامه}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kānat al-lugha akbar ʿaqaba amāmah.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Language was the biggest obstacle in his way.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{عقبة}} (\emph{ʿaqaba}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ʿ-q-b}, \textquotedblleft{}to come after, to follow\textquotedblright{} (Lane). \emph{ʿAqaba} first named a steep mountain road; in modern use it is any obstacle.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ʿaqaba}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ʿaqaba}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kānat al-lugha akbar ʿaqaba amāmah.} — Language was the biggest obstacle in his way.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to contribute, then the Arabic for an incentive, then say \emph{ʿaqaba} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{عقبة} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}An obstacle\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{صعوبة} (ṣuʿūba)}{صعوبة (ṣuʿūba)}]{\ar{صعوبة} (ṣuʿūba) — a difficulty}

\label{lesson:AR-C372-suuba}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for an incentive, then the Arabic for an obstacle.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{صعوبة}}
\textbf{\ar{صعوبة}} — \emph{ṣuʿūba} — \textquotedblleft{}a difficulty\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{وجدت} \ar{صعوبة} \ar{في} \ar{فهم} \ar{الدرس}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{wajadtu ṣuʿūba fī fahm ad-dars.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I had difficulty understanding the lesson.
\end{quote}

\ar{بصعوبة}, \emph{bi-ṣuʿūba}, with difficulty.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{صعوبة}} (\emph{ṣuʿūba}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ṣ-ʿ-b}, \textquotedblleft{}to be hard, difficult\textquotedblright{} (Lane). \emph{Ṣuʿūba} is the verbal noun of the root of \emph{ṣaʿb}, difficult: difficulty.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ṣuʿūba}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{wajadtu ṣuʿūba fī fahm ad-dars.} — I had difficulty understanding the lesson.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for an incentive, then the Arabic for an obstacle, then say \emph{ṣuʿūba} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{معضلة} (muʿḍila)}{معضلة (muʿḍila)}]{\ar{معضلة} (muʿḍila) — a dilemma}

\label{lesson:AR-C372-mudila}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for an obstacle, then the Arabic for a difficulty.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{معضلة}}
\textbf{\ar{معضلة}} — \emph{muʿḍila} — \textquotedblleft{}a dilemma\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{واجهت} \ar{الأسرة} \ar{معضلة} \ar{صعبة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{wājahat al-usra muʿḍila ṣaʿba.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The family faced a hard dilemma.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{معضلة}} (\emph{muʿḍila}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ʿ-ḍ-l}, \textquotedblleft{}to hinder, to make hard\textquotedblright{} (Lane). \emph{Muʿḍila} is a Form IV active participle, feminine: a matter that baffles, a dilemma. \ar{عضلة}, a muscle, is from the same root.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{muʿḍila}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{wājahat al-usra muʿḍila ṣaʿba.} — The family faced a hard dilemma.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for an obstacle, then the Arabic for a difficulty, then say \emph{muʿḍila} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{أخفق} (akhfaqa)}{أخفق (akhfaqa)}]{\ar{أخفق} (akhfaqa) — to fall short}

\label{lesson:AR-C372-akhfaqa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a difficulty, then the Arabic for a dilemma.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{أخفق}}
\textbf{\ar{أخفق}} — \emph{akhfaqa} — \textquotedblleft{}to fall short\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{أخفق} \ar{الفريق} \ar{في} \ar{المباراة} \ar{الأخيرة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{akhfaqa al-farīq fī al-mubārā al-akhīra.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The team fell short in the last match.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يخفق}, \emph{yukhfiq}.

It takes \ar{في}: \ar{أخفق} \ar{في} …. Compare \ar{فشل}, failure.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{أخفق}} (\emph{akhfaqa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{kh-f-q}, \textquotedblleft{}to flap, to beat\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Lane gives Form IV for one who sought a thing and did not get it: to fall short.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{akhfaqa}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{akhfaqa}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{akhfaqa al-farīq fī al-mubārā al-akhīra.} — The team fell short in the last match.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a difficulty, then the Arabic for a dilemma, then say \emph{akhfaqa} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{تمكن} (tamakkana)}{تمكن (tamakkana)}]{\ar{تمكن} (tamakkana) — to manage to}

\label{lesson:AR-C372-tamakkana}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a dilemma, then the Arabic for to fall short.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{تمكن}}
\textbf{\ar{تمكن}} — \emph{tamakkana} — \textquotedblleft{}to manage to\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{تمكن} \ar{الطالب} \ar{من} \ar{حل} \ar{المسألة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{tamakkana aṭ-ṭālib min ḥall al-masʾala.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The student managed to solve the problem.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يتمكن}, \emph{yatamakkan}.

It takes \ar{من}: \ar{تمكن} \ar{من} ….

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{تمكن}} (\emph{tamakkana}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{m-k-n}, \textquotedblleft{}to be firm, to have power\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form V, to become firmly able: to manage to do a thing.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tamakkana}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tamakkana aṭ-ṭālib min ḥall al-masʾala.} — The student managed to solve the problem.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a dilemma, then the Arabic for to fall short, then say \emph{tamakkana} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
